clue.text: Detective's rubbish, taking over, holding criminal down

indicators.note: the first stretch of letters holds the next piece inside it, as hands hold something

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, with the possessive 's giving S

indicators.note: the rubbish word takes the over letter into itself

parts.note: to slate is to criticise harshly, i.e. to rubbish
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
a con is a convict, a criminal

explanation.surface: A police officer's work is trashed while a crook takes over and holds them down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' makes SOLATE, with O inside; 'holding' splits DISSOLATE after DIS. 'down' sits at the end as the definition, meaning miserable rather than a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down means being dejected and inconsolable, a synonym for being miserable.

clue.text: Drill part's end oddly spread

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters, first, third, fifth and so on, of these words

explanation.surface: The tip of a drill bit has strangely splayed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Spread as a past participle means widened or expanded, as a pupil is enlarged.

clue.text: Symbol seen in general mathematics appears initially

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: A sign found in general mathematics turns up at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition fits the surface too: the Greek letter is a common maths symbol for a sum.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek letter S is used as a mathematical symbol, notably for summation.

clue.text: Persistent stink rising and Government keeps cool

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: BO is body odour, a stink

indicators.note: the Government word keeps the cool word inside it

parts.note: the state is the government of a country
in means fashionable, cool

explanation.surface: A lingering smell grows while the authorities stay unbothered.
explanation.definitionFit: Persistent and stubborn both describe someone who refuses to give up or yield.

clue.text: Drink top of sugar syrup

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: syrup of figs is Cockney rhyming slang for a wig, shortened to syrup

explanation.surface: Have a drink of the sweet syrup that sits on top of the sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang, a London habit, makes 'syrup' (from syrup of figs) mean a wig.
explanation.definitionFit: Drink as a noun can mean a gulp or swallow, a large mouthful of liquid.

clue.text: From cellist, 'Les Sylphides' is sluggish

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows it

explanation.surface: A cellist finds the ballet music Les Sylphides a lethargic piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Les Sylphides is a short ballet set to Chopin's music.
explanation.definitionFit: Sluggish and lacking energy or enthusiasm are synonyms for apathetic, lethargic behaviour.

clue.text: Cheers old boy overturning love ban …

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks, like cheers

indicators.note: in a down clue overturning flips the word over, so it is read backwards

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Thanks to an old boy for overturning the prohibition on love.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the surface to the next clue and has no role in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A ban and a prohibition are synonyms; something forbidden by custom is untouchable.

clue.text: … losing head, affair leads to marriage

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a dalliance is a casual love affair

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a fling loses its heady thrill and ends in wedlock.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage is a union or partnership, as is a bond between two families.

clue.text: Twist long hair around girl's extremities

indicators.note: the long hair word goes around the picked letters

parts.note: a mane is a long mass of hair

indicators.note: the extremities of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Twisting long hair round the ends of a girl's tresses.
explanation.definitionFit: To twist something out of shape is to crush or distort it, as a wringer does to laundry.

clue.text: Planning deficit cut takes sense in charge

indicators.note: the shortened deficit word takes the next pieces inside it
cut means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a loss is a deficit
the gist is the general sense of something

explanation.surface: A plan to cut the deficit has the sense to put someone in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Planning and organising the detailed movement of supplies and people is a synonym here.

clue.text: A block turned in wood

indicators.note: turned means the words before it are read backwards

parts.note: a slab is a flat block of stone or wood

explanation.surface: A block of wood has been shaped on a lathe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' suggests woodturning on a lathe, but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The very light tropical timber is a wood used for model aircraft.

clue.text: Sad jerk purchasing Sun?

indicators.note: purchasing means getting hold of, so the jerk word holds the Sun word

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary jerk
The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper, and a rag is a low-quality newspaper

explanation.surface: Only a pathetic fool would buy The Sun.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid, the kind of paper dismissed as a rag.
explanation.definitionFit: Sad in the sense of deeply unhappy or calamitous is a synonym, as in a woeful story.

clue.text: Becoming visible after first appearance of bud?

definitions.text: Becoming visible after first appearance of bud?

indicators.note: after means the becoming-visible word comes after the picked letter
the first appearance of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: looming means emerging into view, often indistinctly

explanation.surface: A flower opening into view once the bud first shows.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a flower opening once its bud has appeared, and also gives the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower opening into view after budding is in flower, the gardener's sense of the word.

clue.text: Square back garden containing borders of furze

indicators.note: back means the whole result is read backwards
the garden word contains the picked letters

parts.note: in American usage a yard is a garden

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A square back garden edged with gorse bushes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' gives YARFED, which 'back' reverses. 'Square' looks like a shape but is the verb meaning settle a bill; 'yard' for garden is American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To square a bill is to settle or pay it, which is a synonym for covering the cost.

clue.text: Soft soap less frothy on baby's bottom

indicators.note: in a down clue X on Y puts X above, so before, Y

parts.note: flatter means having fewer bubbles, less frothy

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Soap that lathers less, used for washing a baby's bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft soap' looks like a toiletry but is the idiom for smooth talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft soap is an idiom for insincere praise used to persuade someone.

clue.text: Caught by dearest, ran to get divorce

indicators.note: caught by says only part of the word dearest is captured, its tail end

parts.note: to range is to extend or run to, as prices range to a top figure

explanation.surface: Captured by a loved one, someone fled to get a divorce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught by' keeps only EST, the tail of 'dearest'. 'ran to' looks like a run of letters to hunt through but is the verb meaning extended to.
explanation.definitionFit: To divorce two things is to separate or alienate them from each other.

clue.text: Blame split about prudish male sharing male

indicators.note: the split word goes about the other pieces

parts.note: to rend is to split or tear apart
prim means prudish and proper

indicators.note: sharing says the male word overlaps its neighbours, so its shared letters are not written twice

parts.note: a man is a male

explanation.surface: A disapproving man and another man split the blame between them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sharing' makes MAN share its M with PRIM and its N with REND, so only A is added. The blog notes this as a setter's slip: the clue was later revised to use 'answer' for A.
explanation.definitionFit: To blame someone formally is to rebuke or censure them, a synonym in the verb sense.

clue.text: Sweet tablet twisted into spiral

indicators.note: the twisted piece goes into the spiral word

parts.note: a loop is a coil or spiral

indicators.note: twisted means the word is turned around and read backwards

parts.note: a pill is a tablet

explanation.surface: A sweet tablet gets twisted into a spiral shape.
explanation.walkthrough: A spiral-shaped sweet on a stick fits the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet here is a confection on a stick, the classic boiled candy for children.

clue.text: One accompanies guy playing, covering Queen

indicators.note: the guy and playing words go around, covering, the Queen abbreviation

parts.note: a chap is a guy
on means playing, as an actor is on stage
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A man performing on stage stands in for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who goes with a young woman to keep her proper is a chaperone, one who escorts.

clue.text: Virgin is pursued, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the words sound like the answer when spoken

parts.note: being pursued means being chased

explanation.surface: A maiden is being followed, so the story goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgin as an adjective means pure and unsullied by sexual experience.

clue.text: Sort of betting from score studied

parts.note: the SP is informal for the score, the latest facts or information
to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: A gambler studies the scores to find a kind of wager.
explanation.definitionFit: In spread betting the punter stakes money on a range of outcomes rather than a fixed result.

clue.text: Fancies gentleman surrounded by revolting offspring

indicators.note: the gentleman word is surrounded by the turned offspring word
revolting means turning over, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: seed means offspring or descendants
Sir is the title of a knight, a gentleman

explanation.surface: A gentleman longs for something while his rebellious children surround him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' gives DEES, and 'surrounded by' signals the container; 'revolting' reads as disgusting or rebellious in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancies as a verb means wants or longs for, the same as wishes or cravings.

clue.text: Like Pharaoh, see keenly

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
Tut is short for Tutankhamun, the boy pharaoh
Ely is a cathedral city and diocese, a bishop's see, in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Like an Egyptian ruler, look with sharp eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; Ely is a cathedral city in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Keenly in the sense of sharply and shrewdly means with quick, clever perception.

clue.text: One's indebted after beginning of tax rise

indicators.note: after means the debtor word follows the picked letter
the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: an ower is one who owes, a debtor

explanation.surface: A debtor faces a tax increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' looks like a tax increase but is the verb to soar.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise high above is to soar or loom over, as a tall building does.

clue.text: Medical containers maintaining temperature for organs

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the containers word holds the temperature letter

parts.note: vials are small glass containers for medicines

explanation.surface: Medical containers kept at a set temperature to store organs for transplant.
explanation.definitionFit: The vital organs of the body, such as heart and lungs, are called this informally.

clue.text: Candid clues occasionally confuse

indicators.note: occasionally means taking only every other letter of the words

explanation.surface: Clues that are only sometimes frank can bewilder a solver.
explanation.definitionFit: To confuse is to muddle or befuddle someone's mind.

clue.text: Mole or spy, they say

indicators.note: they say means the word sounds like the answer when spoken

parts.note: to peer is to look closely, to spy

explanation.surface: Is that agent a mole or a spy, so people claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' looks like a secret agent but is a stone breakwater.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a massive harbour wall or breakwater jutting into the sea, like a jetty.

clue.text: Put out unfinished article facing controversy

indicators.note: unfinished means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: the is the definite article
a row is a quarrel or controversy

explanation.surface: An unfinished newspaper article sparks a dispute and is published.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' looks like publishing but means to disconcert.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone out is to disconcert or unsettle them, as an unexpected question does.

clue.text: Greek character, Hero's lover, missing sweetheart's flirt

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: missing means the heart letter is taken out of the lover's name

parts.note: in Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to reach Hero
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter, E

explanation.surface: A Greek hero's lover, missing his sweetheart, becomes a flirt.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek legend Leander drowned swimming the Hellespont to Hero.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who flirts with many women is a womaniser, the noun sense of flirt.

clue.text: Order peeled cored nectarine in squash

indicators.note: the peeled and cored pieces go in the squash word

parts.note: to press is to squash
pared means peeled, as fruit is

indicators.note: cored means the core is removed, leaving only the outside letters

explanation.surface: Instructions for preparing a nectarine in a fruit drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like an instruction but means a state of readiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in good order, ready for action, is a state of readiness.
